prior_evidence: Criteria file counts (criterion 8 present). Prompt half holds: default.py (diff lines 125-130) keeps the original sentence verbatim in the `else` branch when rule_sets is False, and tests/unit/test_system_prompt.py:786-791 asserts the rule_sets=False prompt equals the default builder's. Catalog-read half has a departure inside the trigger: the PR also changes src/sqllens/safety/rls.py (diff lines 152-187) so apply_rls never matches an [[rls]] rule against a MySQL information_schema.<name> reference (_is_mysql_metadata_relation), independent of any rule-set file. No sibling criterion names it: criteria 1-7 are all 'under the example set', and criterion 8 says reads 'return what they return today'. The test test_without_a_rule_set_catalog_reads_are_unchanged (tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py:662-672) only covers a guard chain without RLS rules, so it does not cover this case. Trigger split: rule_sets False/no file -> prompt branch unchanged (in trigger, conforms); `_is_mysql_metadata_relation` true for information_schema refs with an rls rule named like a view -> departure (needs no fault, fires with no rule-set file). The departure turns an error into a success, so its impact is small.

prior_evidence: The claim's ordering premise is wrong. factory.py:127-132 wraps RlsGuardRunner first (inner), then RuleSetGuardRunner around it (outer), and the comment at 129-130 says 'The rule-set guard sits outside flat RLS'. RuleSetGuardRunner.run_sql (rule_sets.py:603-616) rewrites the SQL first and then calls inner.run_sql, so the rule-set guard runs BEFORE RLS and RLS sees the already-rewritten SQL. So the test and the factory both place RLS inside the rule-set guard. The claim's statement that RLS runs before the rule-set guard is the reverse of the code. I did not execute the test, so I did not check that the byte-identical output assertion holds.
